Provider policy: a configured dRPC key is the standing authorization; collectors take --provider auto --allow-network with no paid-use flags or consent question; step 1, the runbook's network and denial-recovery sections, the backend reference and docs/provider-setup.md say so; the documented start budget is 360 of the 400 ceiling. Backend 3.9.0.
Runbook: the creation transaction comes from the explorer's address page (retried once on a transient failure) or from Sourcify's deployment record; no step or command changes. Backend 3.8.1.

Step 4: start already ran its recommended queue (preset-run lines); the coordinator runs only a deferred row and adds a preset only for a receipt hash a lane found or a contract the user named. Backend 3.8.0.
Rating rules gain the listed-LP-holders clause; step 4 wording unchanged (the queue now starts with positions for GoPlus-listed unread LP ids). Backend 3.7.0.

Step 4: run the printed recommended presets in order (usually none or one); Safe modules/guard, custodian getters and sale receipts are pipeline reads, so a preset is added only for a receipt hash a lane found or a contract the user named. Backend 3.6.0.

Start-failure guidance: network_unavailable (nothing answered) means request network permission for the start command itself, then the identical in-place restart; other transport categories keep the declared-policy check. Backend 3.5.1; no reporting, schema or budget changes.

Deeper targeted verification: the coordinator may order up to four presets (was two) while at least 150 s remain before the deadline, custody first: enumerate the canonical pool's other large positions with logs then positions, read locker withdrawal getters and Safe modules/guard, then receipts and side pools. Guidance only; no backend, reporting or budget changes.

Chain-specific built-in public RPC defaults for seven registered mainnets, explicit credential-free public selection, unchanged configured-provider authorization gates, and target-derived selection for presets and low-level collections. Separate per-command paid flags from repeat consent; exercise clean link/copy installation and report delivery.

Distinguish paid-use approval rejection from general network denial; preserve standing authorization and host boundaries, continue independently permitted public research under required review, isolate public endpoint selection, and complete useful permitted work before requesting missing authorization. Read provider policy in a dedicated output. No backend, reporting, schema or host permission changes.

Publication hardening: anonymous EVM web captures reject private destinations and connected peers, validate redirects, and ignore environment proxies. Claude uses ordinary host tool permissions without shipped auto-allow wildcards.
Accept lossless crypto-token-due-diligence handoffs and preserve the original absolute deadline in collector scheduling; retire native-asset routing to crypto-research.

Distinguish market activity from the receipt-verification sample; lead with evidenced trading activity, acknowledge user-reported execution, and describe untested size-dependent costs as research limits rather than implied selling difficulty.

User asks beyond the address (--focus) and user links (--url, at most six, credential-free) are stored in intake.json and rendered into both lane briefs as 'What the user asked'; the project lane captures the links first, each ask ends as an inference finding or a coverage attempt, and the scaffold echoes user_focus so the verdict answers it

Use declared host network policy before the first collector and lane capture call; request per-command execution permission when required, preserve budgets and honor denial. No global permission changes or additional network probes.

Per-finding native source links (client-rendered company/product icons where available, no emoji substitutes) reused from existing evidence in the current render/read/answer step; local frozen-evidence fallback. No added network requests, tool calls, agent turns, research steps or budget changes.

Production review: bounded retry/redirect/restart accounting, exact same-pool sale matching, missing-data and authority wording, and reliable internal checkpoints. No added research steps, tool calls or agent turns.

Exact unique-address holder aggregates from atomic RPC balances, runtime-shape classification and explicit sample exclusions; existing delivery response preserves coverage beyond optional summary signals. No added network requests, tool calls or agent turns.

Depth without turns: a 6.7-minute live run on 3.1.0 completed with five findings and three Unverified rows because Cloudflare blocked the explorer and the creation transaction was never found; 3.2.0 fixes access and moves the factual half of the report into the pipeline

The pipeline note (eight to ten strongly supported findings from pinned evidence: controls, launch receipt, custodian and Safe, pool depth and quotes, receipt-verified sales, top holders, admin authority, dependencies, maturity) is composed by start; the coordinator assigns topic/signal through `signals`
Report standard: at least eight summary rows, every pipeline-observed dimension rated from observations, a maturity row; Unverified reserved for what pipeline, lanes and presets could not establish
Lane briefs drop the tool-call cap, document the explorer JSON endpoints that answer the fetcher, and point lanes at pipeline-captured holders, transfers and signer activity
Retained from 3.1.0: structured start diagnostics with in-place restart, brief files with pointer prompts, lane compose --check, scaffold, presets and composes chained in one call
Chat delivery renders the four conclusions (technical exposure, credibility and maturity, token economics, research confidence) as four bullets, never one paragraph
validation_scope: Offline public-selection and clean-install tests plus specialist regression suites; live fresh-host acceptance outcomes and limitations are recorded separately in the review record.
